First calculate a fixed monthly payment from the principal, nominal interest rate and whole number of months. Then find the monthly discount rate that makes the present value of all payments equal principal minus upfront fees. The displayed annualized rate is 12 times that monthly rate; the effective annual rate compounds it for a year. At zero interest with no fees, both rates are exactly zero.

This is an adult category reference, not diagnosis or treatment advice. It does not assess children, pregnancy, low blood pressure or the cause of symptoms. Measurement technique and repeated readings matter; a clinician interprets the result with your history.
What do the two numbers mean?
Systolic is the pressure when the heart contracts; diastolic is the pressure between beats. Both matter — the category uses whichever falls in the higher band.
Does one high reading mean I have hypertension?
No. Diagnosis requires repeated elevated readings over time, usually including readings taken outside the clinic. A single high reading is a reason to recheck, not a diagnosis.
Why is my clinic reading higher than at home?
White-coat effect: stress in a clinical setting raises readings for many people. Home readings taken with correct technique are often lower and are part of the diagnostic picture.
How should I measure blood pressure accurately?

Seated, back supported, feet flat, arm at heart height, correct cuff size, no caffeine or exercise in the prior 30 minutes, and a few minutes of rest first. Two readings a minute apart, averaged, beat one rushed reading.
The gap between systolic and diastolic — 50 mmHg in the example. A wide gap can reflect stiff arteries, but it is interpreted alongside the absolute numbers, not alone.
When should I seek urgent care?

A very high reading with chest pain, trouble breathing, weakness, vision changes or difficulty speaking needs emergency help immediately. Without these symptoms, wait at least one minute and measure again. If it remains over 180 systolic or 120 diastolic, contact a healthcare professional promptly.

What is the difference between velocity and acceleration?

Velocity is how fast something moves; acceleration is how fast that velocity changes. A car cruising at a steady 30 m/s has high velocity and zero acceleration; the same car speeding up from 0 to 30 m/s has positive acceleration throughout.
What does a negative acceleration mean?
Because acceleration is velocity change per unit time: (m/s) ÷ s = m/s². It reads as "metres per second, per second" — each second, velocity grows by that many m/s.
How does this relate to force?
Newton's second law: force = mass × acceleration. A 1,000 kg car accelerating at 6 m/s² needs 6,000 N of net force. This page does not ask for mass, so it cannot report force.
Can I use km/h instead of m/s?

BMR is resting expenditure only — it excludes activity, digestion, and exercise, so it is lower than total daily expenditure. It is not a metabolic test and not a personal energy prescription.
The energy the body uses at complete rest to maintain basic functions. Any activity on top of rest adds to it, which is why total daily expenditure is higher.

Yes, through the −5 × age term: each additional year lowers the estimate by 5 kcal/day at fixed weight and height.

Find the units and revenue needed for contribution margin to cover fixed costs.
Every unit sold beyond break-even adds one unit of contribution margin to profit, at these prices and costs.
Fixed costs and variable cost are held at the values above; only the price changes across rows.

Fixed costs $50,000, price $200, variable cost $120: contribution margin is $200 − $120 = $80 per unit, so break-even units = $50,000 ÷ $80 = 625 units, and break-even revenue = 625 × $200 = $125,000.

Price must exceed variable cost, or break-even never arrives. Product mix, taxes, stepped costs that jump at capacity limits, volume discounts, and changing prices are excluded — this is a single-product, constant-price model.
Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (unit price − unit variable cost). It finds the sales volume where total contribution exactly pays the fixed costs.
Then every sale loses money and there is no break-even volume — selling more only deepens the loss. The price must cover the variable cost before fixed costs can be recovered.
Price minus variable cost per unit: the amount each sale contributes toward fixed costs and then profit. Here it is $80 per unit at the example values.
No. Treat the break-even revenue as pre-tax revenue and apply your own tax treatment separately.
No. With a product mix you need a weighted-average contribution margin. This calculator models one product at one price.

MET values are population averages for an activity, not measurements of your session: fitness, technique, equipment, terrain, and individual physiology all shift the true value. It also counts gross expenditure, including the energy you would have used at rest during the same minutes.
A multiple of resting energy cost. Sitting quietly is 1 MET; an activity rated 6 MET is treated as costing six times as much energy per minute.
Because the MET figure is an average across people, and your efficiency, fitness, and equipment differ from that average.

The formula assumes one constant intensity. For mixed sessions, split the time by intensity and add the parts, or treat the result as an average-intensity approximation.
Use a published MET compendium value for the activity as performed — the same activity done harder or with load carries a higher MET.
Area, circumference, and diameter of a circle from its radius, with the formulas shown and worked through.
Enter the radius in any unit — metres, centimetres, inches — and the results come back in that unit (square units for area). Results update as you type. All calculations run locally in your browser.
Area = π × radius². Circumference = 2 × π × radius. Diameter = 2 × radius. π is used at full precision and results are rounded to two decimals for display.
Radius 5: area = π × 5² = π × 25 = 78.54. Circumference = 2 × π × 5 = 31.42. Diameter = 10. If the radius was 5 cm, the area is 78.54 cm² and the circumference is 31.42 cm.

This is a perfect circle: one radius, one centre. Ellipses, arcs, sectors, and rings need their own formulas and are not covered here. The page does not convert units — a radius in inches gives an area in square inches; convert first if you need another unit.
Radius: the distance from the centre to the edge. If you only know the diameter (edge to edge through the centre), halve it first — or read the diameter chip above in reverse.
Because area covers a surface. A radius of 5 cm gives 78.54 cm², not 78.54 cm. Mixing the two is the most common circle mistake.
Full double-precision pi (3.141592653589793…), not 3.14. The difference only matters past the second decimal, but there is no reason to round early.
With the square: doubling the radius quadruples the area. A radius-10 circle has area 314.16, exactly four times the radius-5 area of 78.54.
No. A sphere's surface area is 4πr² and its volume is (4/3)πr³ — different formulas for a 3D object.
Divide it by 2π to get the radius, then enter that here. For a circumference of 31.42, the radius is 31.42 ÷ 6.2832 = 5.
